landmark_cases.title: Gall v. United States
landmark_cases.reason: Sets the modern framework for appellate sentencing review—procedural vs. substantive reasonableness, advisory Guidelines as the starting point, and abuse-of-discretion review.

landmark_cases.title: Rosales-Mireles v. United States
landmark_cases.reason: Emphasizes the importance of correctly calculating the Guidelines and identifies improper calculation as significant procedural error before assessing substantive reasonableness.

landmark_cases.title: Sprint/United Management Co. v. Mendelsohn
landmark_cases.reason: Canonical on trial courts’ broad discretion over relevance and admissibility under Rules 401/403 and the deferential abuse-of-discretion standard on appeal.

landmark_cases.title: United States v. Battle
landmark_cases.reason: Eighth Circuit precedent treating prior possession of the same firearm as intrinsic evidence (not Rule 404(b) propensity) directly relevant to proving possession.

landmark_cases.title: United States v. Goodhouse
landmark_cases.reason: Eighth Circuit application of the presumption that a within-Guidelines sentence is reasonable on appeal, guiding the substantive reasonableness analysis.
